Calculate sleep metrics from diary bed times

Source: R/acti_calculate_sleep_diary_metrics.R
acti_calculate_sleep_diary_metrics.Rd

Scores each diary night from epoch-level sleep/wake data (e.g. from acti_calculate_cole_kripke() or acti_calculate_sadeh()) using the diary's in-bed, sleep-onset, and out-of-bed times, as ActiLife does when bed times are entered from a sleep diary. acti_calculate_tudor_locke() instead detects bed and onset times from the counts, so its latency is always 0.

Usage

acti_calculate_sleep_diary_metrics(
  data,
  diary,
  in_bed_col = "in_bed_time",
  onset_col = "onset_time",
  out_bed_col = "out_bed_time",
  epoch_seconds = NULL,
  check_times = TRUE,
  do_rounding = TRUE,
  rounder = c("round", "Round")
)

Arguments

data

Epoch-level data with a POSIXct time (or timestamp) column, a sleep column ("S"/"W", or logical with TRUE for sleep), and axis1 counts. A vector-magnitude column (counts, vector.magnitude, or vm) is optional and gives activity_counts_vm.

diary

A data frame with one row per night and POSIXct in-bed and out-of-bed times, and optionally sleep-onset times. Without an onset column, onset is the in-bed time. An index column, if present, labels the nights and must be unique. Other columns are kept in the output.

in_bed_col, onset_col, out_bed_col

Names of the diary in-bed, sleep-onset, and out-of-bed columns. Out of bed is exclusive: the epoch starting at out_bed_time is not in bed.

epoch_seconds

Epoch length in seconds. If NULL, it is estimated from time. It must divide 60 seconds (e.g. 15, 30, or 60).

check_times

If TRUE, every in-bed epoch must be in data, so that the diary times are on the epoch grid and there are no gaps.

do_rounding

If TRUE, round efficiency and ave_awakening to 2 digits and the movement and fragmentation indices to 3 digits.

rounder

"round" uses base round() (round half to even); "Round" rounds half away from zero, as ActiLife does.

Value

A tibble with one row per diary night: the diary columns (index, in_bed_time, onset_time, out_bed_time, and any others), then the metrics below. Times are in minutes. The sleep period runs from onset_time to out_bed_time.

latency

Time from getting into bed to sleep onset.

efficiency

100 * total_sleep_time / duration.

duration

Time in bed, from in_bed_time to out_bed_time.

activity_counts, activity_counts_vm

Sum of axis1 and of the vector magnitude (NA if absent) in the sleep period.

nonzero_epochs

Sleep-period epochs with axis1 > 0.

total_sleep_time

Sleep ("S") time in the sleep period.

wake_after_onset

Wake ("W") time in the sleep period (WASO).

nb_awakenings

Number of wake bouts in the sleep period, not counting a wake bout at onset.

ave_awakening

Mean length of those wake bouts (0 if none).

movement_index

Percent of sleep-period epochs with axis1 > 0.

fragmentation_index

Percent of sleep bouts that are at most one minute long (0 if no sleep).

sleep_fragmentation_index

movement_index + fragmentation_index.

Examples

data = actimetrics::acti_count_data
ck = acti_calculate_cole_kripke(data)
diary = data.frame(
  in_bed_time = data$time[5],
  onset_time = data$time[10],
  out_bed_time = data$time[35]
)
acti_calculate_sleep_diary_metrics(ck, diary)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 17
#>   index in_bed_time         onset_time          out_bed_time        latency
#>   <int> <dttm>              <dttm>              <dttm>                <dbl>
#> 1     1 2019-09-17 18:44:00 2019-09-17 18:49:00 2019-09-17 19:14:00       5
#> # ℹ 12 more variables: efficiency <dbl>, duration <dbl>, activity_counts <dbl>,
#> #   activity_counts_vm <dbl>, nonzero_epochs <int>, total_sleep_time <dbl>,
#> #   wake_after_onset <dbl>, nb_awakenings <int>, ave_awakening <dbl>,
#> #   movement_index <dbl>, fragmentation_index <dbl>,
#> #   sleep_fragmentation_index <dbl>
